descriptionChirho: To place or put someone or something under the authority or control of another, used transitively with an agent who causes subjection.
To voluntarily place oneself under the authority of another or to be in a state of subordination, used in the middle voice for willing obedience or deference.
To be made subject or put into subjection by an external agent, often in the theological passive referring to God's eschatological subjection of all things under Christ.
